summary: A text-based interactive mission design game where players balance mass, power, budget, and telemetry constraints to launch and operate real-world NASA-style space missions, learning aerospace engineering trade-offs through branching scenarios.
details:
Overview

Orbital Compromise is an accessible, text-driven interactive game designed for students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Instead of requiring high-end graphics, the game focuses on the core intellectual challenge of aerospace engineering: managing strict resource budgets and making critical trade-offs under uncertainty.

How It Works

Players act as Lead Mission Architects. Across five structured mission phases—Objective Selection, Spacecraft Assembly, Launch & Orbit Insertion, Deep-Space Anomaly Response, and Post-Mission Telemetry Analysis—players choose hardware modules and operational strategies. Every decision directly impacts five core engineering parameters: Budget ($M), Mass (kg), Power Generation (W), Data Throughput (Mbps), and Mission Lifespan (Years).

Educational & Scientific Value

Using realistic mission parameters inspired by NASA and partner agency datasets (such as Lunar South Pole reconnaissance and Earth climate observation), the game demonstrates why engineers cannot simply "pick the best parts." Overloading a satellite breaks the launch vehicle mass limit, while high-resolution instruments drain power reserves during eclipses. At the end of each playthrough, players receive a detailed Engineering Debriefing explaining the physics and mission logic behind their success or failure.

Format & Accessibility

Built as a branching hypertext playbook, Orbital Compromise can be played on any device without installation, making it ideal for classrooms, workshops, and independent learners worldwide.
